Definition: genitive (i.e. possessive) of G846, used as an adverb of location; properly, belonging to the same spot, i.e. in this (or that) place:--(t-)here.
BiblicalUsage: This is the possessive form of the same pronoun — his, its, theirs — used as an adverb of place, meaning belonging to the same spot. Paul left Priscilla and Aquila there at Ephesus, and Jesus told his disciples to sit there while he went to pray.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe even a word this small reminds me that God works in particular places, with particular people, not in abstractions.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
